setting: the hill at twenty past eight on the morning after the third night, already warm, traffic building below him, his breathing audible on the descent, one long stop where he says nothing for eleven seconds and then only says that it is going to be hotter today, a bin lorry braking somewhere out of sight, the last sentence given up on halfway

the art room after six with the corridor show finally hung, chairs going up onto tables one at a time between sentences, the desk fan running flat behind her voice, a tap left on and then turned off, her voice tired and pleased and going too fast when she describes one drawing, keys picked up at the end

the grass verge outside a marquee at twenty to ten at night, a band muffled through canvas behind him, plastic chairs being stacked in a rhythm, a car door and gravel, wind across the microphone twice, his voice lower than usual and slower, one long silence where he only listens to the band and lets it run

the bottom of the hill on the last morning of june, cooler air and birds instead of heat, a bus pulling away, the roster mentioned twice and a paper bag rustling in his hand, the word july said once flatly and then said again as if testing it, footsteps stopping at a crossing and starting again
